text:
maria_chen: Heads up — onboarding sampleapp failing on embeddings/rerank parity. Node SDK (v0.9.3) sometimes returns payloads with null `vector` keys when the batching helper sends a batch of length == 1. Python SDK returns the expected shape. Repro steps below.

ashwin_gupta: Can you paste the exact request body you used and the raw response? Are you using the sampleapp’s batching helper (lib/batcher.js) or rolling your own?

maria_chen: Using the sampleapp helper. Minimal repro:
```json
POST /v1/embeddings/batch
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>

{
  "model": "open-vec-1",
  "inputs": ["why is my vector null?"],
  "metadata": {"session_id": "onboard-42"}
}
```
Server returns: 
```json
{
  "results": [ null ]
  // expected: [{ "embedding": [ ...float32s... ], "id": "<uuid>" }]
```
No error field, just null entry. :facepalm:

ashwin_gupta: Interesting. That null looks like we dropped mapping for that position after a retry/merge. Can you reproduce with a single direct curl (no SDK) to rule out helper bug?

maria_chen: Direct curl -> always returns correct embedding. Node SDK repro only when workload causes a token refresh during a request (we're hitting the auth refresh path).

samir_k: That rings a bell. We saw a subtle race: when the auth layer refreshes token mid-batch, the retry wrapper can re-dispatch a subset of items; the server merges fragments but our client-side zipper assumes a 1:1 mapping and ends up inserting nulls for missing indexes. TL;DR: token-refresh + partial retry -> misaligned index map.

liz_devx: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) SDK: make batching helper attach an `id` per input (stable uuid) and reconstruct by id instead of index; 2) sampleapp: add a guard that retries the entire batch if any nulls are returned; 3) docs: call out that null result means an internal mapping error and encourage enabling verbose logs. I'll draft a PR.

ashwin_gupta: Agreed on stable ids. Quick patch (works locally): in batcher.js wrap each item as `{ id: nanoid(), payload: <original> }` and on response do a lookup by id. Stops the index-sensitivity.

maria_chen: Patch confirmed — sampleapp passes now even while forcing token refresh in dev environment. Thanks! Will run longer smoke test.

devex-bot: PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/sdk-node/pulls/1289 — "batcher: use stable ids to reconstruct responses; handle null entries gracefully" — automated tests queued. :white_check_mark:

samir_k: Follow-up: we should also harden the auth retry behaviour. Right now refresh lock allows two inflight requests to race while one refreshes, causing duplicate partial dispatches. I'll add a small debounce/lock in auth client so that in-flight refreshes block other calls until complete. That plus stable ids should be robust.

liz_devx: I'll add an integration test to the sampleapp harness that simulates transient auth failures during batching and asserts no nulls and idempotency. Also adding a small note in the onboarding guide under "Embedding shape and retries".

ashwin_gupta: For immediate workaround for customers: patch the sampleapp config flag `BATCHER_SAFE_BY_ID=true` and restart. We'll surface that in the status channel and the onboarding checklist.

maria_chen: Verified with three different models and both rerank/embeddings endpoints — stable ids + auth lock fixes the nulls. Leaving this thread as resolved for now but please tag me on the PR if anything flakey pops up. :thumbsup:

samir_k: I'll monitor CI and infra metrics for any leftover anomalies. If we still see partial nulls, we'll enable request-level tracing to correlate token refresh events with batch boundaries.

liz_devx: Filed docs ticket: DOCS-482 "Embedding responses: null entries and retry semantics". Also adding a small sample snippet on how SDKs should validate response shapes.

maria_chen: Great work folks. Moving to follow-up items in the PR and docs tickets.
